mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen monotonically from -64.1 to -58.0 over the last four weeks, a steady 6.1-point recovery trend. This momentum reflects an ongoing unwinding of movement restrictions that should continue mechanically into the next four weeks absent a new shock.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved every week from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than or equal to the mean over the last 28 days despite the four-week monotonic uptrend observed here.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL time has fallen steadily from 19.7 to 17.1 over four weeks, indicating households are spending less time confined at home. Once RESIDENTIAL drops below a 15-point threshold, discretionary out-of-home behavior typically accelerates, lifting retail and recreation visits within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 15 points above baseline
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined from 19.7 to 17.1 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise within two weeks of RESIDENTIAL crossing below 15 points, or RESIDENTIAL stalls above 15 without crossing.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has recovered from -46.0 to -41.4 over four weeks, consistent with phased reopening of offices under eased Delhi lockdown policy. This commuting recovery is expected to continue feeding adjacent retail and recreation footfall over the next four weeks as reopening policy persists.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -46.0 to -41.4 across four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to increase over the next 28 days even though WORKPLACES continues its upward trend, falsifying the reopening transmission mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT (-58.7 to -55.3) and WORKPLACES (-46.0 to -41.4) are both recovering simultaneously. When both commuting-linked series rise together, their combined effect on enabling physical access to retail venues is larger than either alone, producing an amplified two-week RETAIL_REC increase beyond what either series predicts individually.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both rise for two consecutive weeks simultaneously
evidence_refs: fact:both series improved every week over the snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC growth over the next two weeks is no larger than the growth predicted from TRANSIT or WORKPLACES alone (i.e., no super-additive effect), rejecting the interaction claim.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has climbed from -86.6 to -82.6, still deeply negative. If PARKS crosses above -80, it signals a meaningful behavioral shift toward outdoor and public-space comfort that typically spills over into nearby retail and recreation visits within one week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises above -80 points from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose from -86.6 to -82.6 over four weeks, approaching the -80 threshold
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise in the week following a PARKS crossing above -80, or PARKS never crosses the threshold while RETAIL_REC still rises, invalidating the trigger linkage.

mechanism_narrative: July in Delhi falls within the monsoon season, during which heavy rainfall historically suppresses outdoor shopping and recreation trips regardless of policy reopening. This seasonal dampening is expected to flatten or reverse the recent RETAIL_REC recovery over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:decision date is 2020-07-15, within Delhi monsoon season
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to rise over the next 28 days at a pace comparable to or faster than the prior four weeks, showing no monsoon-linked suppression.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has improved steadily from -31.0 to -25.3, indicating essential-trip normalization. Historically, narrowing of essential-trip deficits precedes a broader normalization of discretionary retail and recreation trips within two weeks as household risk tolerance rises.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved every week from -31.0 to -25.3
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve within two weeks despite continued narrowing of the GROCERY_PHARM deficit, breaking the presumed lead-lag relationship.

mechanism_narrative: Under an active reopening regime, simultaneous improvement in TRANSIT access and decline in RESIDENTIAL confinement jointly enable both the means and willingness to travel for retail, producing a compounded four-week RETAIL_REC increase that neither series alone would generate in a non-reopening regime.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT improves and RESIDENTIAL declines in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rose from -58.7 to -55.3 while RESIDENTIAL fell from 19.7 to 17.1
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise in weeks where TRANSIT improves and RESIDENTIAL falls concurrently, or the joint effect is no larger than either series acting alone, rejecting the interaction mechanism.
